# Visual Workflow-Automation FOSS Platforms — iPaaS, Flow Programming, AI Builders, BPMN and the n8n Ecosystem (2026-09)

**Scope.** Self-hostable, open or source-available platforms where automation is authored on a visual surface — node canvases, trigger-action builders, BPMN modelers, block graphs. Code-first orchestrators that offer visual monitoring but code authoring (Airflow, Prefect, Dagster, Kestra, Temporal, Inngest) are deliberately excluded and named here; Trigger.dev is tabled as that family's honest boundary row. Proprietary services (Zapier, Make, Pipedream, Workato) and domain-specific platforms (Home Assistant) are out of scope. Verified as of 2026-09-22.

**Companions:** `oss-categories-report-2026-09.md` (65-category main report) · `infinite-canvas-foss-tools-2026-09.md` (canvas engines and AI canvases) · `uiux-design-prototyping-tools-2026-09.md` · `ui-component-libraries-2026-09.md` · `browser-android-scraping-deep-dive-2026-09.md` · `kb-distillation-tools-2026-09.md` · `codebase-teardown-tools-2026-09.md`.

**The 2026 landscape.** Two facts define the year. First, gravity moved to agents: read the repositories' own descriptions and nearly every platform now leads with AI — n8n describes itself as fair-code with native AI capabilities, Activepieces' description opens with AI agents and MCP servers, Trigger.dev brands around durable AI agents, and the LLM-native builders (Dify, Langflow, RAGFlow, Flowise, Sim, Coze Studio) have collectively overtaken the classic iPaaS generation in stars. n8n itself, at more than two hundred thousand stars, now ranks among the largest repositories in all of open source; the tailwind behind it is agents, not calendars and webhooks. The tail of the table shows the frontier dissolving in both directions: natural-language agents that drive the computer with no canvas at all, and MCP servers that let coding agents author the visual workflows for humans.

The counter-thread, as in this series' canvas report, is licensing. The fair-code question n8n embodied has spread: Activepieces, Windmill, Automatisch, Flowise, Dify, Automa and bpmn-js all register non-standard license files on GitHub in 2026 — custom cores with commercial carve-outs or branding requirements — while Langflow kept MIT through its corporate journey, and Coze Studio, RAGFlow, Sim, Trigger.dev, StackStorm and Flowable hold Apache-2.0. Two lineages ended: Camunda 7's community edition was archived with its successor on source-available terms, and TIBCO's Flogo has been frozen since 2024. And one rename happened live during this report's verification: Motia transferred to `iii-hq/iii` and, at check time, shipped no license file at all.

**Method.** Candidate discovery from the source listings corpus (385-video showcase + Product Hunt viewer) and ten retained research-toolkit searches on the free DDG engine (roundups, license comparisons, flow programming, BPMN engines, browser automation, agent builders; cached in `scratch/pages/workflow-search.jsonl`; an earlier 14-query pass was discarded to a result-parser mismatch — no paid engine was reachable at any point). **Every tabled repo was health-verified via `gh api` on 2026-09-22** ($0 toolkit spend). Rows marked ＋ are web-researched; unmarked rows also appeared in the source listings. Verification resolved live events: `motiadev/motia` now redirects to `iii-hq/iii`, `camunda/camunda-bpm-platform` is archived with Camunda 7 declared end of life, and Activepieces' license — still marketed as MIT in third-party roundups — registers non-standard on GitHub today.

---

## A. General-purpose automation platforms

The self-hosted iPaaS family: wire SaaS events, APIs and internal tools together on a canvas. **n8n** (★206k) dominates by ecosystem — hundreds of native integrations, code nodes when the canvas runs out, and an AI pivot that made it the default substrate for agent workflows. **Activepieces** (★25k) is the agent-flavored challenger now leaning hard into MCP servers; **Automatisch** keeps the Zapier shape for simplicity-first teams; **Windmill** turns scripts into flows for infra-minded shops; **Huginn** (★50k, MIT) is the Ruby agent-zoo classic that predates them all and still ships; **Trigger.dev** is the boundary row — code-defined workflows with a visual console, included because it is where teams go when canvas authoring stops scaling.

## B. Event-driven & flow-programming platforms

The older, deeper tradition: flow-based programming for events and devices. **Node-RED** (★24k, OpenJS Foundation, Apache-2.0) remains the reference — a palette-and-wire canvas that owns IoT, hardware and edge wiring, with a decade of community nodes behind it. **StackStorm** (Apache-2.0) is its ops sibling: sensors, rules and action chains for auto-remediation and incident response. **Flogo** (⚠ frozen since 2024) is the Go heritage row — light enough for the edge, now a snapshot rather than a project. The section is small but it is the load-bearing one: this is the lineage the AI builders above quietly inherit their canvas grammar from.

## D. BPMN & process automation

The enterprise tradition: long-lived, stateful business processes rather than event wiring. **Flowable** (Apache-2.0, ★10k) is the active standard-bearer of the Activiti lineage, executing BPMN, CMMN and DMN with visual modelers. **Camunda 7 CE** (⚠ archived November 2025) ended its run — its own description now points to Camunda 8, which is source-available rather than open, making the archived repository the last free artifact of the line. **bpmn-js** is the canvas library beneath countless custom process tools — free to embed with a watermark-attribution requirement, the BPMN world's React Flow.

Where n8n and its peers wire SaaS events together, Flowable models long-lived business processes — approvals, cases, decisions — with visual modelers in the BPMN tradition and an engine built for state that outlives a browser session. ## E. Browser-automation canvases & the n8n ecosystem

Where automation meets the browser and the agents. **Automa** (★22k) puts the block canvas inside a Chrome or Firefox extension — scheduled page automation with no server. **Skyvern** (AGPL-3.0, ★23k) drives browsers with natural-language agents under a visual workflow builder. The last three rows are the n8n ecosystem as an infrastructure layer: **n8n-MCP** (★23k, MIT, pushed yesterday) lets Claude Code, Cursor and Windsurf build n8n workflows programmatically — agents authoring the canvas — the **Zie619 collection** (★57k) packages thousands of ready-made workflow JSONs, and the **Self-hosted AI Starter Kit** is n8n's own Compose template for a local AI stack: the fastest on-ramp to running this whole section on your own hardware.

## Recommendations by intent

- **Wire SaaS and APIs together, self-hosted.** **n8n** if fair-code terms are acceptable — the deepest integration catalog and the largest community; **Activepieces** as the agent-first alternative (mind its now-custom license file); **Automatisch** for Zapier-shaped simplicity, noting its early-2026 pause.
- **Hard FOSS requirement.** **Node-RED** (Apache-2.0, OpenJS Foundation) and **Huginn** (MIT) for classic automation; **Langflow** (MIT) for AI flows; **Flowable** (Apache-2.0) for business processes.
- **Build AI agents visually.** **Langflow** or **Flowise** for graph-style composition; **Dify** when RAG pipelines and agents belong in one workspace (license: review); **Coze Studio** for an all-in-one Apache-2.0 platform; **Sim** for team collaboration; **RAGFlow** when retrieval quality is the core requirement.
- **Agents in code, visual operations.** **Trigger.dev** — durable agents and workflows in TypeScript with a proper console.
- **Events, devices and ops.** **Node-RED** for IoT and edge wiring; **StackStorm** for auto-remediation and incident response; **Flogo** only for maintaining existing Go edge flows (frozen).
- **Stateful business processes.** **Flowable** as the engine; **bpmn-js** to embed a modeler in your own app; **Camunda 7** only for maintenance — it is archived.
- **Automate the browser.** **Automa** for in-extension block flows; **Skyvern** for natural-language browser agents; pair with **n8n-MCP** to have coding agents build the n8n side for you.
- **Start locally with real models.** The **Self-hosted AI Starter Kit** — one Compose command, then evaluate section C tools against your own stack.
